m.d: When you know something, you have facts or ideas in your mind.
m.e: I knew more things after I went to school.

m.d: You know a person, if you have met him or her.
m.e: Yes, I know John. I met him in class last week.

m.d: In algebra, a variable or constant whose value is already determined.
Any fact or situation which is well-researched or familiar.
If something is known, people know about it; it is famous.
m.e: It is a known fact that water freezes at 0°C.

m.d: A sound from something hard hitting wood.
An impact.
When you knock on something, you hit your knuckles onto it repeatedly.
m.e: She knocked on my door three times before I opened it.

m.d: When you knock something, you hit it, often accidentally.
A knife is a tool that cuts.
m.e: He ate with his knife and fork.

m.d: A knife is a tool with a thin edge.
m.e: He worked with a putty knife.

m.d: If you knife someone, you stab someone with a knife; you make a hole in them.
m.e: The gang knifed him sixteen times.

m.d: A knowing look or smile tells someone that you know something.
m.e: "All set. Have a good weekend," she said with a knowing smile.

m.d: Knowledge is information that you know.
m.e: He shared his knowledge with you.

m.d: A knight was a man who fought in battles on a horse during the Middle Ages.
m.e: The knights rode up to the castle and broke in.

m.d: A knight is a person who has been given knighthood by a king or queen.
A chess piece, often in the shape of a horse's head, that is moved two squares in one direction and one at right angles to that direction in a single move…
Part of the leg between the thigh and the shin.
m.e: I hurt my knee in football.

m.d: To hit someone or something with the knee.
m.e: He kneed me in the leg.

m.d: If you kneel, you lower your body and put one or two of your knees on the floor.
m.e: In many religions, people kneel when they pray.

m.d: A knot is formed when a rope is tied.
m.e: He put a knot in the rope.

m.d: A knot is a unit of speed.
To create a tied place in a cord or rope.
m.e: They knotted the ends of the rope together.

m.d: A knob is a rounded handle on a door or drawer.
Knickers refers to the underwear (a piece of clothing) that is worn by a female.
If you have a knack for doing something, you have a special skill or ability to do it easily.
m.e: He has a knack for fixing computers.

m.d: A knack is a trick or a clever way of doing something.
m.e: The door sticks, but there's a knack to opening it.

m.d: When you knit, you make a cloth from a long wool thread, usually by hands with needles.
m.e: My mother loves to knit beautiful scarves for me to wear.

m.d: A knuckle is the joint of a finger, especially the bottom joint of a finger.
If you do something knowingly, you know you are doing it.
m.e: It was not an accident -- he knowingly installed a virus in our computer.

m.d: If you act knowingly, you show that you know something.
m.e: He looked at me knowingly, and I knew he was not fooled.

m.d: If a person is knowledgeable that person knows many things, or a great amount about something.
m.e: She is very knowledgeable when it comes to medicine.

m.d: In the game of cribbage, knobs is the Jack of the same suit as the card that was revealed after the deck was cut.
